vault.title: Lab 01 - Image basics (numpy)
vault.summary: This document outlines the first lab assignment for an Introduction to Computer Vision course. Students will learn to treat images as NumPy arrays by building a synthetic 64x64 RGB gradient image from scratch. The five tasks cover creating color gradients, converting to grayscale, cropping and flipping via array slicing, computing intensity histograms, and applying mean-intensity thresholding with ASCII art output. The final deliverable is a Jupyter Notebook named lab01.ipynb to be submitted on WSP.
key_terms: NumPy: A library for numerical computing in Python used here to manipulate image arrays.
Grayscale: An image format where each pixel represents a single intensity value.
Array Slicing: A Python feature to extract sub-regions of arrays without using loops.
Histogram: A graphical representation of the distribution of numerical data, such as pixel intensities.
Thresholding: A technique to segment an image by converting grayscale pixels into binary values.

vault.title: CSCI3240 Introduction to Computer Vision Syllabus
vault.summary: This document outlines the 15-week schedule, lab sessions, and grading policy for CSCI3240 Introduction to Computer Vision, taught by Abenova Saule. Students will learn core computer vision topics ranging from image processing and filtering to feature detection, stereo vision, and deep learning. Assessment is based on labs (30%), a midterm exam (30%), and a final project (40%).
key_terms: Convolution: A mathematical operation used in linear filtering for image processing.
Canny: A popular edge detection algorithm.
SIFT: Scale-Invariant Feature Transform for detecting and describing local features.
Homography: A transformation relating the coordinates of points in two images.
RANSAC: An iterative method to estimate mathematical model parameters from noisy data.
CNN: Convolutional Neural Network used for image classification and computer vision tasks.

vault.title: CSCI3240 Introduction to Computer Vision - Lecture 01: Introduction
vault.summary: This document introduces the Introduction to Computer Vision course taught by instructor Abenova Saule at KBTU. It covers the course overview and grading policy, fundamentals of images as arrays defined by height, width, channels, and uint8 data type. It also outlines the essential Python tools used in the course, including numpy, OpenCV, and matplotlib.
key_terms: Images as arrays: representation of digital images using height, width, and color channels
dtype uint8: unsigned 8-bit integer data type commonly used for pixel values
numpy: library for numerical computing in Python
OpenCV: library specialized in computer vision tasks
matplotlib: plotting library used for data visualization
